agent: attach wave reader A - the unit panel's attach, detach and create-headquarters buttons
question: What the single unit panel's attach_button, detach_button and four create_* buttons do when pressed; the window attachment_selection_panel and its rows (CUnitAttachmentEntry); the multi-unit CCreateHigherCommand constructor; what a player's create_theatre makes.

addresses.name: CSingleUnitButtons::OnAttachButton
addresses.comment: **`attach_button`'s click** (glue +0x130, registered at 0x75D298). Nothing under the custom-game lock (0x4208B0). Otherwise **any window already at +0x2C is thrown away - window slot 20, the object freed - and a new CUnitAttachmentPanel(screen, unit) always made** and stored at +0x2C, so a second press rebuilds the window and shows it, it does not shut it. Ghidra prints the destroy as a whole else branch with an early return; the listing (0x75E694..0x75E6C7) falls through into the construction. No Update or anything else of CSingleUnitButtons reads +0x2C, so the window lives until the next press or until the strip is destroyed (its destructor 0x75D8A0 does the same throw-away), which happens whenever CSingleUnitPanel::Rebuild or CSingleUnitPanel_Hide empties the panel's list. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-attachbuttons.md.
addresses.evidence: Read off the listing 0x75E650-0x75E780 (ret 4) and the registration at 0x75D298 (attach_button with lea eax,[esi+0x130]; glue +0x130 is the push of 0x75E650 at 0x75D0C3). Would be shown wrong by another writer of +0x2C or a reader outside the two named.

addresses.name: CSingleUnitButtons::OnDetachButton
addresses.comment: **`detach_button`'s click** (glue +0xE0, registered at 0x75D2F3). Nothing under the custom-game lock (0x4208B0); otherwise **one CDetachUnitCommand(the unit)** (constructor 0x5DE1D0, 0x64 bytes) posted to the session (the in-game screen's slot 18 at +0x48, its +0x38 channel, slot 6). No test of its own and nothing else: selection and panel are left alone. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-attachbuttons.md.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x75D9D0-0x75DAD9. The only constructor called is 0x5DE1D0. Would be shown wrong by a further call between the post and the ret.

addresses.name: CSingleUnitButtons::OnCreateHigherButton
addresses.comment: **The click of all four `create_*` buttons** - one handler, the glue at +0x180 registered on `create_corps`, `create_army`, `create_armygroup` and `create_theatre` (0x75D570 to 0x75D681). Nothing under the custom-game lock (0x4208B0), or where a custom game's test 0x420EB0 says no; otherwise **one CCreateHigherCommand(the unit)** - the one-unit constructor 0x5DF320, which leaves +0x54 (select) at 0 so the new headquarters is not selected - posted. **No test of level, parent or manpower here**: those are the button's enabling (CSingleUnitButtons::Update) and the command's own IsValid. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-attachbuttons.md.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x75DAE0-0x75DBFC; `push 0x58; call 0xb9602f` is the 0x58-byte command, `call 0x5df320` the one-unit constructor (argument the unit at [esi+0x28]). Would be shown wrong by a second call to a create-specific routine.

addresses.name: CUnitAttachmentPanel::CUnitAttachmentPanel
addresses.signature: CUnitAttachmentPanel* __fastcall CUnitAttachmentPanel::CUnitAttachmentPanel(CInGameIdler* screen@ECX, CUnitAttachmentPanel* this@stack:4, CUnit* unit@stack:8) @EAX
addresses.comment: **The window a unit picks its headquarters in.** A class with no RTTI of its own, named from CButtonObserverGlue<CUnitAttachmentPanel>, 0x34 bytes: +0 the window `attachment_selection_panel`, made by the screen's CEU3Gui (slot 14) slot 11 with the screen's slot 16 as the second argument; +4 the unit; +8 the glue (the file's `back_button`, click CUnitAttachmentPanel::OnBack). **Candidates are every unit of the unit's owner (CCountry +0xBAC, all levels) for which CUnit_MayTakeSubordinate(candidate, unit, 0) says yes**, no limit of distance or province, each put in order by CUnitAttachmentPanel_InsertSorted with the unit written to the static 0x1A85628 first. The list box `list` is emptied (slot 23), one CUnitAttachmentEntry per candidate added in the sorted order, and the window shown (CGuiObject slot 13). Nothing here pauses the game or positions the window: it stands where the file says. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-attachbuttons.md.
addresses.evidence: Decompilation and listing 0x76EF70-0x76F244 (ret 8). CButtonObserverGlue<CUnitAttachmentPanel> vftable 0x15D8998 is written at +8. Would be shown wrong by a position-setting or pause call - there is no such call in the body; the calls are the window factory, the two string assigns, FindButton, the country accessor 0x402610, MayTakeSubordinate, InsertSorted, FindListBox, the entry constructor and Show.

addresses.name: CUnitAttachmentPanel::OnBack
addresses.comment: **`back_button`'s click**: the panel's window hidden (its +0x18 CGuiObject, slot 14). The object is not destroyed here - the unit's strip keeps it at +0x2C until the next press of `attach_button` or until the strip is destroyed. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-attachbuttons.md.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x76F250-0x76F25D, ret 4, referenced only at 0x76EFB6 as the glue's click. Would be shown wrong by a window slot other than Hide at +0x38.

addresses.name: CUnitAttachmentPanel_SortsAfter
addresses.comment: **Whether candidate `a` is to come after candidate `b`** in the attachment list. The unit being attached is the static 0x1A85628. Where that unit is land (slot 15): a after b where a's oob_level < b's. Otherwise: a after b where a's oob_level > b's. **Then, in both, where the level did not answer true - equal levels and the other way round alike - the distance alone**: a after b where CMap::DistanceBetweenProvinces(the unit's province, a's) > (the unit's province, b's). So it is not a clean lexicographic order and the insertion below is the whole rule. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-attachbuttons.md.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x76EEE0-0x76EF6D, ret 4. The jge at 0x76EF07 and the jg at 0x76EF1D both lead to the same distance block at 0x76EF1F. Would be shown wrong by a further comparison before the distance; there is none.

addresses.name: CUnitAttachmentPanel_InsertSorted
addresses.comment: **Insertion from the tail**: node = the tail; while node and CUnitAttachmentPanel_SortsAfter(node's unit, the new unit), node = node's previous. No node left: the new unit is put at the head (CList_PushFront). Otherwise it is put straight after that node. Called with the units of CCountry +0xBAC in that list's order. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-attachbuttons.md.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x770790-0x7707C2 and on, ret 8; the loop walks +4 (previous) from +4 of the list header (the tail). Would be shown wrong if +4 of the node were the next link; the head-insert arm and the walk both fix it as previous.

addresses.name: CUnitAttachmentEntry::CUnitAttachmentEntry
addresses.signature: CUnitAttachmentEntry* __stdcall CUnitAttachmentEntry::CUnitAttachmentEntry(CUnitAttachmentEntry* this, CUnitAttachmentPanel* panel, CInGameIdler* screen, CUnit* candidate, CUnit* subject)
addresses.comment: **A row of the attachment list, 0xD0 bytes**: the window `unit_assignment_entry`, +0x28 a CRef to the candidate, +0x50 a CRef to the unit being attached, +0x78 the panel, +0x80 the glue of the button `assign` (click CUnitAttachmentEntry::OnAssign). `name` the candidate's name (slot 7). `location` the name of the candidate's province, then ` (`, then CMap::DistanceBetweenProvinces(candidate's province, the unit's province) in decimal, then `km)` - both literals, not localised. `counter_type` the sprite `GFX_counter_` + the candidate's first brigade's definition key (+0x58, +8), where the intel level (+0x1F8) is 3 or more and it has a brigade with a definition, else the empty suffix; set only where such a sprite exists. `counter_size` the frame by oob_level: level 0 six, 1 five, 2 four, 3 three (a candidate is never below that), plus the arms for 4 and 5 that do not arise. `unit_pride_star` frame 3 where the first brigade's `+0xA5` (pride) is set. The class has no tooltip slot of its own (its first table has 12 slots) and no per-frame update. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-attachbuttons.md.
addresses.evidence: Decompilation and listing 0x76E4E0-0x76EC25, ret 0x14; the +0x1F8 read at 0x76E99A, the size switch on +0x1F4, the pride read through the first regiment. Would be shown wrong if +0x1F8 were not the intel level the record has for it.

addresses.name: CUnitAttachmentEntry::OnAssign
addresses.comment: **A row's `assign` button.** Resolves the two CRefs to the candidate (+0x28, its cached pointer refreshed) and the unit (+0x50), builds **CAttachUnitCommand(unit, candidate)** (0x5DE890; the row's candidate is the parent), posts it to the session, and hides the panel's window (`[+0x78]` -> window, +0x18, slot 14). It tests nothing itself. The window object stays until the strip is destroyed - which the command's result brings about, CSingleUnitPanel_RefreshIfChanged seeing the count of units above differ and rebuilding the panel. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-attachbuttons.md.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x76ED40-0x76EED8, ret 4; pushes at 0x76EDE3/0x76EDE4 are the parent then the unit, then the object at 0x76EDED. Would be shown wrong by a different argument order; CAttachUnitCommand's constructor is (this, unit, parent).

addresses.name: CCreateHigherCommand::CCreateHigherCommand_Units
addresses.comment: **The several-units constructor**, posted by CInGameIdler::OnHigherCommandMultiUnit with the vector CInGameIdler_CollectForHigherCommand filled. `units` is a pointer to a vector of CUnit* ({begin, end} read). As the one-unit constructor (0x5DF320) in every step but two: the id pair reserved the same way under the same spin lock, and the counter moved on by 3, but **+0x54 (select) is 1** - so CCreateHigherCommand::Execute, for the local player, selects the new headquarters with the screen's Select - and every unit of the vector appended as a CRef to +0x3C rather than one. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-attachbuttons.md.
addresses.evidence: Decompilation 0x5DF430 onward, ret 8 (`*(undefined1 *)(param_1 + 0x15) = 1`). Sibling of the one-unit constructor at 0x5DF320, which writes 0 there. Would be shown wrong by a caller that reads +0x54 as something other than the select flag; CCreateHigherCommand::Execute reads it just before the Select (step 7 of its record).

addresses.name: g_AttachmentPanel_SortSubject
addresses.comment: The unit whose headquarters is being chosen, written by CUnitAttachmentPanel::CUnitAttachmentPanel just before its loop and read by CUnitAttachmentPanel_SortsAfter, which has no other way to be told. Written once per panel. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-attachbuttons.md.
addresses.evidence: Written at 0x76F092 (VA of the instruction) and read at 0x76EEE3 and 0x76EF1F. Would be shown wrong by another writer.

structs.name: CUnitAttachmentPanel
structs.comment: The window a unit picks its headquarters in. No RTTI of its own (its members' CButtonObserverGlue<CUnitAttachmentPanel> names it). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-attachbuttons.md.
structs.evidence: `push 0x34; call 0xb9602f` at 0x75E6C7 is its one allocation site; the constructor writes +0..+0x30 inclusive and +8 runs 0x2C bytes.

structs.name: CUnitAttachmentEntry
structs.comment: A row of the attachment list: the window `unit_assignment_entry`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-attachbuttons.md.
structs.evidence: `push 0xd0` at 0x76F139 is its one allocation site, and vftable 0x15D89C4 (rva 0x11D89C4) is what the RTTI export gives as its primary table.

structs.name: CSingleUnitButtons
structs.comment: The strip of buttons under a selected unit: the window `sup_buttons_window`, an entry of CSingleUnitPanel's list. Layout of its glue objects is in CSingleUnitButtons::CSingleUnitButtons. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-unitpanel.md, section 9.
structs.evidence: vftable 0x15D8D80 written by its constructor at 0x75CF99, and by its destructor at 0x75D8BE; RTTI's primary table.

struct_fields.comment: The window `sup_buttons_window`, as the entry pattern of the unit panel has it (CUnitView +0x20).
struct_fields.evidence: Written at 0x75CF6B from the factory call that made `sup_buttons_window`.

struct_fields.name: unit
struct_fields.evidence: `mov [esi+0x28], ecx` at 0x75CF93 from the constructor's unit argument, read by every handler.

struct_fields.name: attachment_panel
struct_fields.comment: The attachment window this strip made, or null. Replaced whole by each press of attach_button (CSingleUnitButtons::OnAttachButton) and thrown away by the destructor; nothing else touches it.
struct_fields.evidence: Written at 0x75E76D; read at 0x75E694 and at 0x75D8D2 (the destructor). A grep over Update found no other reader.

struct_fields.comment: The in-game screen handed to the constructor in ECX.
struct_fields.evidence: `mov [esi+0x30], edi` at 0x75CF90, edi the constructor's ECX.

struct_fields.name: window
struct_fields.evidence: `mov [edi], eax` at 0x76F01F from the window factory.

struct_fields.name: unit
struct_fields.comment: The unit whose headquarters is being chosen.

struct_fields.comment: The CButtonObserverGlue<CUnitAttachmentPanel> of `back_button`, 0x2C bytes embedded; its callback is CUnitAttachmentPanel::OnBack.
struct_fields.evidence: The glue is built in place at +8 and handed to back_button at 0x76F064.

struct_fields.name: window
struct_fields.evidence: Written at 0x76E57C from the window factory.

struct_fields.evidence: The reference builder 0x42DD70 at 0x76E5B7 with the candidate; resolved and used as the parent by OnAssign.
